clue.text: Article used by waiters and linesmen on B.R.

definitions.text: Article used by waiters and linesmen on B.R.

parts.words: Article used by waiters and linesmen on B.R.
parts.note: read as two compound words: a dish waiters carry seafood on, and the steel bar railway linesmen bolt across rail joints

explanation.surface: A puzzle over some piece of kit shared by restaurant staff and British Rail track workers.
explanation.walkthrough: B.R. is British Rail, the old national railway; its linesmen maintain the track. The waiters' article is a plate for fish, and the railwaymen's is the bar joining two rails end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a serving dish for seafood and the metal splice bar that joins rail ends on a railway track.

clue.text: Protected circuit and fed us inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the word us is placed within the word fed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes wiring safely, then adds that they fed a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts US within FED, splitting it after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical circuit that has a fuse fitted is protected against overload, so a fused circuit is a protected one.

clue.text: Fight to reserve place for treasured memories

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or fight
to book is to reserve, as a table or a seat

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel over who gets to book a seat somewhere nostalgic.
explanation.definitionFit: An album of pasted cuttings and photos keeps keepsakes, a place where cherished mementoes are stored.

clue.text: Source of energy for authority and growth

parts.note: power means authority or control
a plant is something that grows, a growth

explanation.surface: A political slogan about where real energy comes from: control and expansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A generating station produces electricity, the source of the energy supplied to homes and industry.

clue.text: Effort that tempts partially

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that any try is only half-tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' signals the run hidden across 'thAT TEMPTs'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try, an effort made to achieve something.

clue.text: Cost of putting swans in river

indicators.note: in tells us the swans are put within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite crossword river
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much it costs to release swans onto a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan (a cob is the male). The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Expense is outlay, the money something costs.

clue.text: Short instructions

explanation.surface: A terse set of orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means short in duration; a brief is also the set of instructions given, as to a barrister.

clue.text: Article in plot could be part of necklace

indicators.note: in tells us the article is placed within the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as for flowers
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something found buried in a garden plot might come from a broken necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is often a string of small pierced balls, each one threaded on the cord.

clue.text: Suffer at home with dog

parts.note: being in means being at home
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone endures life cooped up indoors with a mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it, bringing it on yourself.

clue.text: Stuffing with strength of flesh

parts.note: force means strength or power
meat is animal flesh used as food

explanation.surface: A cook describes a filling made with the might of solid flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a seasoned mixture of chopped meat used for stuffing poultry and the like.

clue.text: Fodder in a way uncooked

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: Animal feed served in a fashion that is not cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in a way' as 'somewhat'; here 'way' is ST (street) and 'in' puts RAW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried stalks of cereal are given to livestock as feed and bedding, a basic fodder.

clue.text: One who kicks his heels for a living

definitions.text: One who kicks his heels for a living

parts.words: One who kicks his heels for a living
parts.note: the idiom kicking your heels means idling, but here the heels literally click and strike the floor as a professional performer

explanation.surface: Someone who seems to be paid to loaf about waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'kick your heels' is to wait idly; the clue reads it literally, as a performer in metal-tipped shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: This stage performer strikes the floor rhythmically with metal-plated heels and toes as their trade.

clue.text: Drive crazy about drink in carriage

indicators.note: about tells us the drive-crazy word goes round the drink

parts.note: to dement is to drive mad
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Being driven mad by alcohol while travelling in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' is how one holds oneself, not a coach; 'about' wraps DEMENT round PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deportment is bearing or posture, the way a person carries themselves.

clue.text: Release soldiers in iron

indicators.note: in tells us the soldiers are placed within the iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Freeing troops who have been held in irons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To free is to release, letting someone go.

clue.text: Fly policeman and poison container

explanation.surface: A tangle of an insect, a constable and a vial of poison, like a murder mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: a big buzzing fly, old slang for a police officer (from the blue uniform), and the coloured bottle chemists used for poisons.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a large blowfly, is dated British slang for a constable, and as two words a blue glass vial that marked poison.

clue.text: Doctor going to work allowed a small quantity of liquid

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A physician is permitted to dispense a tiny dose.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a tiny drop, a very small amount of fluid.

clue.text: Drawing dull plain

parts.note: dead means dull or lifeless
level means flat, like a plain

explanation.surface: A sketch of a featureless flat landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' looks like a sketch, but it is a match tied; the surface's 'dull plain' gives the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides drawing a match are exactly even, with scores tied all square.

clue.text: Cuts between Orientals in shadow

indicators.note: between tells us the cuts sit within the pair of Orientals

parts.note: E is east, so two Orientals give two Es
clips are cuts, as with shears

explanation.surface: Trims made among Eastern people in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orientals' is plural, so it gives E twice, one either side of CLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse casts one body into the shadow of another, so the word can mean an overshadowing.

clue.text: Divided up share with editor

parts.note: a portion is a share

explanation.surface: Someone split the profits with a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To portion something is to divide it into shares, so portioned means split up.

clue.text: Request broken cane that's awry

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to repair a broken walking stick that is bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CANE to ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look sideways or obliquely, so the word suggests something off-line, crooked.

clue.text: God I've to follow in eating away

indicators.note: I've is placed to follow the god, after it

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
taken as written

explanation.surface: A believer pledges to follow a deity while being slowly consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts I'VE after EROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erosive wears material away gradually, as water and wind do to rock.

clue.text: Seaside entertainer makes supports collapse

parts.note: a pier is a pillar that supports a structure
rot is decay or collapse

explanation.surface: A clown at the beach whose act brings the pier down.
explanation.walkthrough: PIER stands for 'supports' in the sense of a supporting pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a white-faced clown figure who performed in troupes at British seaside resorts.

clue.text: Officer Commanding surrounded by journalists in operation

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the officer sits within the journalists

parts.note: the press is a collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: A commander mobbed by reporters during a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a series of steps, an operation carried out to a result.

clue.text: Learner and star producing decorative textile

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A trainee and a champion make a fancy fabric together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an openwork fabric of fine threads used for ornament.

clue.text: Swear it could be a remedy around the south

indicators.note: around tells us the remedy goes round the south

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A frustrated person swears that a southern remedy might work.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, using bad language.

clue.text: Mad reason for engine

parts.note: loco is slang for mad
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A crazy reason to want a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway engine that pulls a train is this vehicle.

clue.text: Blunder in terrorism

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies inside the next word

explanation.surface: A mistake made during a campaign of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' shows the run inside 'tERRORism'.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: A great number may accept Pole

indicators.note: accept tells us may takes the pole inside it

parts.note: taken as written
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Lots of people might welcome a Polish visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but a magnetic pole, N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: Many means a large quantity, numerous.

clue.text: Poetry about twisted tail capable of many uses

indicators.note: about tells us poetry goes round the rearranged tail

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters of tail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem about a twisted tail that can serve many purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns TAIL into ATIL, and 'about' puts VERSE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable to many functions or activities is versatile.

clue.text: Voice from irate Norseman

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shout from an angry Viking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the run across 'iraTE NORseman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singing voice above baritone.

clue.text: Cunning dance back to your leader

indicators.note: back tells us the dance word is read in reverse

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: your leader is the first letter of the word your

explanation.surface: A sly dance returns to the head of your group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REEL into LEER, then 'leader' takes the first letter of 'your', Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means knowing and wary, alert in a canny way.

clue.text: Cockney holiday about complete

indicators.note: about tells us the holiday goes round the word for complete

parts.note: Easter is a spring holiday
to end is to complete or finish

explanation.surface: A Londoner's holiday is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a native of London's East End, an inhabitant of that district.
